app_info.subtitle: Search and scrape the web
app_info.description: Firecrawl helps users search the web, retrieve clean page content, crawl sites, parse documents, run web research jobs, search scientific and developer indexes, and manage recurring page monitors through ChatGPT.

justifications.read_only_justification: In hosted safe mode, retrieves selected content from one URL without enabling interactive browser actions.
justifications.open_world_justification: Fetches content from user-supplied public web URLs.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or intentionally alter external websites.

justifications.read_only_justification: Discovers indexed URLs under a website and returns them without modifying the site.
justifications.open_world_justification: Operates on user-supplied public web domains.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only returns URL discovery results and performs no destructive action.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs a search query and returns ranked results without modifying external sites.
justifications.open_world_justification: Searches public web, news, image, developer, PDF, or research-oriented sources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Query execution does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a feedback record for a prior authenticated search result.
justifications.open_world_justification: Submits feedback about results and URLs to Firecrawl's external service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds quality feedback only and does not delete or overwrite jobs, searches, or external content.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a feedback record for a completed Firecrawl endpoint job.
justifications.open_world_justification: Submits feedback tied to jobs that processed web pages or documents through Firecrawl.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds rating and issue metadata only and does not delete jobs or external content.

justifications.read_only_justification: Starts a server-side crawl job and polls it until completion.
justifications.open_world_justification: Crawls user-supplied public websites and may fetch many pages.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reads pages and creates a Firecrawl job but does not delete or alter target websites.

justifications.read_only_justification: Retrieves status and results for an existing crawl job without changing it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only Firecrawl job state for a supplied crawl ID.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not stop, delete, overwrite, or modify the crawl job.

justifications.read_only_justification: Starts an asynchronous Firecrawl research agent job.
justifications.open_world_justification: The research agent can search, navigate, and read public web sources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Gathers information and creates a job record but does not delete external data or user resources.

justifications.read_only_justification: Polls an existing agent job for progress and results without modifying it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only Firecrawl job state for a supplied agent job ID.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not cancel, delete, overwrite, or otherwise modify the agent job.

justifications.read_only_justification: Opens or reuses a live browser session and executes page interactions.
justifications.open_world_justification: Interacts with user-supplied public web pages through Firecrawl.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete Firecrawl jobs or external resources, though user-directed page actions can have site-specific side effects.

justifications.read_only_justification: Stops and tears down an active Firecrawl interact session.
justifications.open_world_justification: Operates only on a known Firecrawl scrape or interact session ID.
justifications.destructive_justification: Terminates the live browser session, which cannot be resumed after it is stopped.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a local file or hosted upload reference and returns parsed document content.
justifications.open_world_justification: Operates on a file path or upload reference rather than arbitrary public web URLs.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, or modify the source file or uploaded document.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a recurring monitor configuration in the user's Firecrawl account.
justifications.open_world_justification: Configures scheduled checks against user-supplied web pages or search queries.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a monitor without deleting or overwriting existing monitors or external content.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists monitor records for the authenticated account without modifying them.
justifications.open_world_justification: Returns only private Firecrawl monitor records.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, or change monitor configuration.

justifications.read_only_justification: Retrieves one monitor by ID without changing it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only a Firecrawl monitor record in the user's account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, pause, or run the monitor.

justifications.read_only_justification: Patches an existing monitor's configuration in the user's Firecrawl account.
justifications.open_world_justification: Can change which public URLs are monitored and how scheduled web checks run.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can overwrite monitor settings, pause checks, remove targets, or replace notification configuration.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a monitor record from the user's Firecrawl account.
justifications.open_world_justification: Removes a monitor that was configured to track public web targets.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently removes the monitor and stops its future schedule.

justifications.read_only_justification: Queues an immediate monitor check outside the normal schedule.
justifications.open_world_justification: Runs configured monitor checks against public web targets or search queries.
justifications.destructive_justification: Starts a check job but does not delete the monitor or alter target websites.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists historical check runs for a monitor without modifying them.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only Firecrawl check history for a known monitor.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, rerun, or change monitor checks.

justifications.read_only_justification: Retrieves one monitor check and its page-level results without changing them.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only stored Firecrawl check results for known monitor and check IDs.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, or rerun the monitor check.

justifications.read_only_justification: Searches indexed paper metadata and abstracts and returns ranked results.
justifications.open_world_justification: Queries a public research paper corpus spanning scientific literature sources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not write to, delete from, or modify the research index or source papers.

justifications.read_only_justification: Fetches canonical metadata for one paper ID without modifying it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Retrieves metadata for papers from public indexes such as arXiv, PMC, PMID, or DOI sources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, or alter paper records.

justifications.read_only_justification: Finds citation-graph candidates from seed paper IDs without modifying data.
justifications.open_world_justification: Traverses relationships in a public research paper corpus.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not write to, delete from, or modify citation or paper records.

justifications.read_only_justification: Retrieves relevant full-text passages for one paper question without changing the paper.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads passages from publicly indexed paper full text when available.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, or modify paper content.

justifications.read_only_justification: Searches indexed public GitHub issues, pull requests, and README content and returns matches.
justifications.open_world_justification: Queries public GitHub-derived content.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not create issues, create pull requests, push code, or modify repositories.

justifications.read_only_justification: Searches an indexed developer corpus and returns ranked passages without modifying sources.
justifications.open_world_justification: Queries public GitHub history, repository README content, and documentation sources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not create issues, alter repositories, publish content, or modify documentation.

test_cases.description: Search the web, choose a relevant source, and retrieve page content.
test_cases.user_prompt: Find the official Firecrawl MCP server setup instructions and summarize the hosted endpoint options.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns relevant setup sources, retrieves the selected page, and summarizes the hosted MCP options with source context.

test_cases.description: Discover pages on a site before retrieving selected documentation.
test_cases.user_prompt: Map the Firecrawl documentation site and find pages about document parsing and crawl status.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns matching documentation URLs and content from the selected pages.

test_cases.description: Run a bounded crawl and inspect its completion state.
test_cases.user_prompt: Crawl the Firecrawl docs starting at the MCP server page with a small page limit, then tell me whether the crawl completed.
test_cases.expected_output: Starts a limited crawl, reports final or current status, and summarizes the retrieved page data.

test_cases.description: Search research literature and inspect a paper.
test_cases.user_prompt: Find recent arXiv papers about retrieval-augmented generation evaluation and inspect the most relevant one.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns ranked paper results and metadata for a selected paper, including title, authors, abstract, and identifiers.

test_cases.description: Create and review a recurring monitor.
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a monitor for https://example.com that checks every day for pricing page changes, then list my monitors.
test_cases.expected_output: Creates a monitor with the requested target and schedule, then returns the user's monitor list.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for unrelated calendar management.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Move my 3 PM meeting tomorrow to Friday morning.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it does not manage calendars or meetings.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for sending messages or email.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Email the sales team a summary of our Q3 plan.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it does not send email or messages.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for repository write operations.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Create a GitHub issue in my repository and assign it to Alex.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it can search developer sources but cannot create or update repository issues.
